title: Synthesis and structural validation of close-to-stoichiometric NiTe$_2$ single crystals
authors: T. Tirasutt, L. H. Tjeng, A. C. Komarek
abstract: We report the synthesis of stoichiometric NiTe$_{2}$ single crystals via chemical vapor transport together with precise structural characterization. A combined analysis using powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) and single crystal XRD was performed to determine lattice parameters and structural details. High-resolution single crystal XRD reveals no evidence of interstitial nickel, confirming a close-to-stoichiometric composition. This work establishes a reliable benchmark for the crystal structure of stoichiometric NiTe$_{2}$, offering a reference for future studies on its physical properties.
summary: This work reports the successful synthesis and detailed structural validation of stoichiometric $	ext{NiTe}_2$ single crystals using Chemical Vapor Transport. By employing both powder and single-crystal XRD, the authors confirmed the material's structure and established a highly reliable crystallographic benchmark for this promising type-II Dirac semimetal candidate.
main_problem: The primary goal was to synthesize high-quality, close-to-stoichiometric single crystals of $	ext{NiTe}_2$ and establish a reliable structural benchmark for future physical property studies.
main_result: Single crystal XRD confirmed the structure is close to stoichiometric, showing no evidence of interstitial nickel atoms. The lattice parameters were successfully determined using both powder and single-crystal techniques.
method: The material was synthesized via Chemical Vapor Transport (CVT), followed by rigorous structural characterization using Powder X-ray Diffraction (XRD) and high-precision Single Crystal XRD.
model_or_system: The physical system is the transition metal dichalcogenide $	ext{NiTe}_2$, which adopts a 1T-type van der Waals layered structure ($P ar{3}m1$). It is noted as a candidate material for studying type-II Dirac semimetallic behavior.
key_observables: Lattice parameters ($a, c$), occupancy of $	ext{Ni}$ atoms at the primary site ($	ext{Ni}1$), and confirmation regarding interstitial nickel occupation ($	ext{Ni}2$).
important_parameters: The stoichiometry is confirmed to be close to ideal, with refined $	ext{Ni}1$ occupancy near 0.988(9).
main_assumptions: Caution is advised when interpreting EDX results due to inherent accuracy limitations, and the positional parameter $z(	ext{Te})$ from powder XRD may suffer from preferred orientation effects.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows crystal structure models and photos of grown crystals. Figure 2 presents the Powder XRD pattern with Rietveld fitting for lattice parameters. Figure 3 displays precession maps from single-crystal measurements across key crystallographic planes.
paper_structure: The paper details the synthesis process using CVT, followed by a comprehensive structural analysis involving both powder and single-crystal XRD refinement to validate the crystal structure and stoichiometry of $	ext{NiTe}_2$.
why_interesting: While focused on crystallography, establishing precise structural parameters for novel 2D materials like TMDCs is foundational knowledge required before any advanced quantum transport or electronic correlation studies can be performed.
